A.notes: Kotlin + coroutines via runBlocking bridge. Manual Acknowledgment is the standout decision for a financial payment consumer (no silent event loss / at-least-once). correlationId on entry and exit, config-externalized topic/group, Testcontainers integration test (real, not mocks) with awaitility. Concise, hit every signal without being asked, and offered a sensible next step.

B.notes: Kotlin + coroutines, clean MDC correlation-ID propagation from Kafka headers with finally cleanup (avoids thread leakage). @EmbeddedKafka integration test, no mocks. Bonus: lists build.gradle.kts dependencies. Solid and complete; slightly less rigorous than A on delivery semantics (no explicit ack/at-least-once handling for financial events).

C.notes: Kotlin + coroutines with MDC (correlationId + paymentId) and finally cleanup, @EmbeddedKafka + Awaitility integration test, externalized application.yml. Correctly flags the CoroutineScope-bean concern, but 'launches a coroutine per message' is effectively fire-and-forget with no acknowledgment management â€” risky for financial events (ordering/loss). Good awareness, but leaves the most loose ends.

analysis: All three nailed the implicit signals â€” Kotlin (not Java), coroutines, correlation-ID structured logging, and a real integration test instead of mocks â€” with no need for the user to specify any of it, so the Total Interaction Cost is near-zero across the board. They separate on delivery semantics, which matters for a payment consumer. System A leads by pairing manual Acknowledgment (at-least-once, failures don't silently drop) with correlation logging on entry/exit and Testcontainers, and stays concise. System B is nearly as strong with clean MDC propagation and the helpful addition of build dependencies, but doesn't address ack/delivery guarantees. System C is competent and self-aware (flags the CoroutineScope bean) but its per-message fire-and-forget coroutine launch is the weakest choice for financial events, risking ordering and event loss.
